(See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary The current visit summary in the expanded queue table row used to show a hard-coded "Scheduled for today" and an "On time" tag for every patient. This PR replaces both with real data, to hopefully show useful information to whoever is managing the queue: **Today's appointments.** A new "Today's appointments" section replaces the previous "Scheduled for today" text, to give more actionable information than an ambiguous "Scheduled for today" that isn't very helpful. It lists the patient's appointments for today from `POST /appointments/search`, one line per appointment: > Checked in · General Medicine at 11:00 AM with Ali Khan +2 providers - Hovering over "+N providers" shows the names of the other providers. Providers removed from the appointment (response `CANCELLED`) and providers without a name are left out, and the names are sorted so the same provider always shows first. - When the patient has no appointments today, the section shows "No appointments scheduled for today". - Nothing is shown while the appointments are loading or if the request fails. - The statuses shown are set by the existing `appointmentStatuses` config, which has been unused since its table was removed in #1729. Its default is now `Scheduled`, `CheckedIn`, `Completed` and `Missed`, and it is validated against the appointment statuses the backend supports. **Visit attribute tags.** The tags next to the visit type now come from the visit's attributes, in the same way as the visit attribute tags in the patient chart banner. A new `visitAttributeTypes` config lists the attribute types to show, and defaults to the Punctuality and Insurance Policy Number types from the reference application demo data. So the punctuality entered in the start visit form now shows here as "On time", "Late" or "Early". The visit custom representation now requests `attributeType.datatypeClassname` so the values can be formatted by datatype (concept, date, or text). ## Screenshots When there are no appointments to show - With multiple appointments that have multiple providers - ## Related Issue [https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-6098](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-6098) ## Other Implementations that still set `appointmentStatuses` from the old scheduled appointments table will now see those statuses in the current visit summary. body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration. - [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary `PersonAttributeField` draws text, coded and location person attributes, but not dates, which openmrs-core supports through [`AttributableDate`](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-core/blob/015b9c67043f0585d0ed6a99b46793fc46fa03a2/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/util/AttributableDate.java#L31). A date such as a consent date therefore had to be a text attribute typed in freely, and an attribute type of a date format showed "Patient attribute type has unknown format". Attribute types of format `org.openmrs.util.AttributableDate` or `java.util.Date` now get a date picker (`OpenmrsDatePicker`). - The value is saved in the `YYYY-MM-DD` format that `AttributableDate` uses. The REST API stores a person attribute's value as it is sent, so the picker is what keeps it in that format. - Selecting a date marks the field as touched, as the date of birth field does, so changing only this date still triggers the unsaved-changes warning. - The field supports the existing `allowFutureDates` and `allowPastDates` field definition options, which until now only applied to date obs fields. - When editing a patient, the REST API returns a saved date as an ISO date-time (`2026-09-20T00:00:00.000+0000`). The initial form values convert it back to `YYYY-MM-DD`, so saving the patient unchanged keeps the value as it was stored. Tests: `person-attribute-field.test.tsx` covers both formats, checking that a selected date is saved as `YYYY-MM-DD` and marks the field as touched (so the discard warning shows), that a saved date is shown, and that `allowFutureDates: false` stops the picker at today. `patient-registration-hooks.test.tsx` checks that a loaded date attribute is converted to `YYYY-MM-DD` while a text attribute is left as loaded. ## Screenshots | Before | After | |---|---| | | | ## Related Issue https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-6040 ## Other This replaces #2808, which closed when its branch was renamed to the ticket number.

- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

`getErrorMessage` now returns the response body when the server sends a plain-text error, instead of falling through to `err.message`.

When a response isn't JSON, `openmrsFetch` sets `responseBody` to the raw text. Some queue module endpoints send plain-text 400s. For example, `POST /queueutil/assignticket` returns "One of the required fields is empty" or "The request could not be interpreted" (with a `Content-Type: application/json` header, but the body isn't JSON). Once https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-management/pull/2789 routes Call action failures through `getErrorMessage`, those snackbars would otherwise show the generic `OpenmrsFetchError` message ("Server responded with 400 (Bad Request) for url ... Check err.responseBody...") instead of the server's reason.

Proxy error pages (like an nginx 502/504) also arrive as a string `responseBody`, so the plain-text body is only used when it's non-empty, 500 characters or fewer, and doesn't contain markup. Otherwise we fall back to `err.message` as before. Structured JSON error fields still take priority.

## Screenshots

https://issues.openmrs.org/browse/O3-5666

## Other

Follow-up to https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-management/pull/2789#discussion_r4157433588. The ticket assignment flows only use `getErrorMessage` once #2789 merges, so that should land first.

The Call row action and the Serve button in the call modal both fire `POST /queueutil/assignticket` without handling a rejection. A failed request becomes an unhandled promise rejection: a full-screen error overlay in dev builds and a click that does nothing in production.

- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Retrying a patient save after a partial failure repeats identifier work that already succeeded. Every retry asks the identifier source for a new value, so a new patient uses up an extra identifier on each attempt. When editing an existing patient, the retry adds identifiers that are already attached. For unique identifier types that addition fails with a 400, so the save can't succeed until the page is reloaded.

Record generated identifier values and completed identifier additions on the save transaction manager, keyed by identifier field name. Reuse a generated value on retry unless the identifier's source changed, and skip additions that already succeeded, so a retry only repeats the work that failed.

Tested against a local backend by failing a save and retrying. A new patient keeps the OpenMRS ID generated on the first attempt, whether the create call or a later step like saving a relationship failed, and an existing patient's retry saves without adding the new ID Card twice.

body:

- [x] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below.

## Summary

With `searchAddressByLevel` enabled, changing a parent address level left the child values from the previous selection in place, so the form could end up with inconsistent addresses (for example, Uganda with Nairobi as the province).

`useAddressEntryFetchConfig` took `setFieldValue` from `usePatientRegistrationContext()`. Every address level renders inside `AddressComponentContainer`, which provides its own `PatientRegistrationContextProvider` whose `setFieldValue` is `async () => {}`. `updateChildElements()` therefore ran on every selection and did nothing.

A 200 whose body is not the expected array is thrown, so SWR reports it through `error` and the components' existing error states render — `AddressComponent` shows its "Error occurred fetching ordered fields for address hierarchy" notification instead of crashing. The derived arrays also fall back to `[]`, so a malformed response can never throw at a consumer.

## Summary

**Before:** on some distros the patient registration page never renders at all — the user gets a white screen instead of a form, with `Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')` in the console. The addresshierarchy module serves `getOrderedAddressHierarchyLevels.form` from a legacy `.form` handler that content-negotiates: asked with `Accept: */*` it returns the expected JSON array, but asked with a browser-style `Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml,...` it returns a **200 carrying an OpenMRS HTML page**. `openmrsFetch` parses the body inside a try / catch, so that response resolves as a *success* with `data` left `undefined` and no error set. `useOrderedAddressHierarchyLevels` then derived `orderedFields` from `data?.data?.map(...)` with no fallback, and `AddressComponent` guards only the loading and error states — so `orderedFields` was `undefined` and `Object.fromEntries(orderedFields.map(...))` threw while rendering, taking the whole registration form down with it.

**After:** the form always renders. If that request comes back with a body that isn't the expected JSON array, the address section shows its existing "Error occurred fetching ordered fields for address hierarchy" inline notification (the error path the component already had) instead of crashing, and the rest of registration stays usable. A well-formed response behaves exactly as before.

**How:** `address-hierarchy.resource.tsx` now wraps `openmrsFetch` in a small shared fetcher that checks the parsed body is an array and throws otherwise, so a non-conforming 200 reaches SWR's `error` rather than masquerading as an empty result — which is what the component's existing `errorFetchingFieldOrder` guard is for. The derived arrays (`orderedFields`, `entries`) also get an `?? []` fallback so no consumer can ever call `.map`/`.slice`/`.findIndex` on `undefined`; that also removes four `'orderedFields' is possibly 'undefined'` errors that `tsc` was already reporting on these files. The same fetcher is used for the other three addresshierarchy `.form` endpoints in the file, which have the same hazard and whose consumers already render an error state.

Note on scope: the durable fix is for the addresshierarchy module to expose a **proper REST API**, and making `openmrsFetch` itself reject or handle a non-JSON `Content-Type` is being handled upstream in `openmrs-esm-core` by a core maintainer. This PR is neither of those and doesn't try to be — it is the defence-in-depth layer that stops the registration form from white-screening in the meantime, and it stays correct once either of those lands.

None — no intentional UI change. The visible difference is the existing address-hierarchy error notification appearing where the form previously failed to render.

Prior art: O3-5631 / #2508 in this repo proposed a similar guard and was closed on the grounds that `openmrsFetch` already parses JSON and this endpoint guarantees `{results: []}`. - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Fixes two problems in the advanced patient search. Follow up to #2702 

### Pagination reverted to page 1

Selecting page 2 would snap back to page 1 a moment later.

`usePagination` rebuilds `goTo` whenever `totalPages` changes, and the search page reset the page with `useEffect(() => goTo(1), [query, goTo])`. Because the search appends result pages in the background, `totalPages` kept growing, `goTo` kept getting a new identity and the effect kept firing. The reset now runs only when the query itself changes.

### Search was slow

The search loaded the entire result set 50 rows at a time, each request waiting on the previous one, before the first 20 rows settled. Measured with a probe against the old code: a 500-result query took **10 serialised round trips**; a 1700-result query took 34.

`useInfinitePatientSearch` now fetches pages with SWR's `parallel: true`, and the advanced search requests them in waves of 4 rather than walking the set one page at a time. A 1700-result query now costs **10 round trips instead of 34**, with at most 4 requests in flight.

Two smaller fixes:

- `totalCount=true` was sent on *every* page request, but only page 1's count is ever read, so now only page 1 asks for it. On this path the count is the size of the list the search handler already built in memory, so this doesn't save a backend query; it just asks for what we use.
- `totalResults` read the count from `data[0]`, which under `keepPreviousData` is the *outgoing* query's page so it reported the previous query's count during a query change. It now reads the count for the current query.

## Summary

Patient edits could report success while name, identifier, or person-attribute deletions were still running. The deletion paths discarded their promises, and attribute deletion also caught failures and only logged them. A failed cleanup could therefore leave stale patient data behind after the UI reported a successful save.

## Summary

Marking a deceased patient as alive sent `dead: false` but omitted the death metadata fields. Because the existing non-null death date remained stored, OpenMRS continued to return `dead: true`, along with the stale death date and non-coded cause of death.

The cause is that omitting a property is not the same as clearing it. When `isDead` is false, `getPatientDeathInfo` returned only `dead: false` and left the death fields out of the payload entirely. OpenMRS clears the coded `causeOfDeath` by itself, but it retains `deathDate` and `causeOfDeathNonCoded` when those properties are absent from the update. Sending explicit nulls is what actually clears them.

This sends `null` for `deathDate`, `causeOfDeath` and `causeOfDeathNonCoded` when the patient is not dead, mirroring the style the `isDead: true` branch already uses when it nulls whichever cause-of-death field does not apply. The person payload types are widened to permit null, and `causeOfDeathNonCoded` is added — it was missing from the type altogether even though the `isDead: true` branch has always sent it.

**Scope.** This is confined to `getPatientDeathInfo` and the death-related types. It does not touch `getDeletedNames` (O3-5910, #2693) or the unawaited `forEach` around `deletePersonName` (O3-5913), both of which live in the same file and are being handled separately.

One test outside those files changed: the payload assertion in `patient-registration.test.tsx` matches `person` exactly rather than partially, so it had to record the three new properties. Without that the existing test fails. It has the side benefit of pinning the new payload at the render-to-request level.

Tests cover both levels the ticket asks for: a unit test that the generated payload contains `dead: false` plus the three explicit nulls, and a request-level test asserting on the body actually handed to `savePatient`. Both fail without the fix. The coded and non-coded cause-of-death paths are also covered so the `isDead: true` behaviour stays pinned.

## Summary

This is patient data loss on every edit. Opening an existing patient who has a local-language name, changing any unrelated field and saving silently destroys that name — the user never touches the local-language option, and nothing in the UI indicates anything was removed.

`getDeletedNames()` returned the existing additional-name UUID whenever one was present, without consulting `values.addNameInLocalLanguage`. Since that flag is still set for any patient who has such a name, the name was scheduled for deletion on every save.

The mechanism is worse than an unwanted delete. `getNames()` already rebuilds the additional name using the same UUID, so each edit updated the name and then deleted it — the two statics disagreed about what to do with one UUID. This changes `getDeletedNames()` to take `values`, mirroring the neighbouring `getNames(values, patientUuidMap)`, and to return the deletion only when `addNameInLocalLanguage` is no longer set, so both functions read the flag from the same place. Checking for a falsy value also covers the `undefined` that `getFormValuesFromFhirPatient` produces when a patient has no additional name.

**Scope note.** The deletions are dispatched through `forEach` with an async callback, so the save reports success before they finish. That is O3-5913, which is assigned, and it is deliberately untouched here — only the predicate and the arguments at its single call site change, so the two fixes compose cleanly. Because the deletion is not awaited today, the tests assert on what `getDeletedNames()` returns rather than on the async side effect; it is a pure function, which is what makes it the right seam.

Tests cover the acceptance criteria: an unrelated edit preserves the name, editing the name updates it (asserted against `getNames()`, showing the same UUID is reused), disabling the option removes it, and a patient with no local-language name produces no deletion. body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration. - [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary The queue wait-time column rendered durations with a hardcoded "(s)" suffix, so it showed "1 minute(s)" and "1 hour(s) and 0 minute(s)". That reads awkwardly in English and cannot express languages with more than two plural forms such as Polish, Arabic, and Russian, so it is effectively unlocalizable. This delegates the formatting to the framework's `formatDurationBetween`, backed by `Intl.DurationFormat`. It decomposes the wait into hours and minutes and applies each locale's own plural rules and connector, so English shows "2 hours, 30 minutes", Polish "2 godziny i 5 minut", and Arabic uses its dual form, with no translation keys to maintain. Setting `minutesDisplay: 'always'` renders a zero-length wait as "0 minutes" natively. Because pluralization now lives in the platform, this removes the `hourAndMinuteFormatted` and `minuteFormatted` keys and adds none. The queue tests cover the wiring (elapsed time from `startedAt`, and preferring `endedAt` when it's set); plural correctness is `Intl`'s responsibility and is tested in esm-core. ## Screenshots ### Before ### After #### Plural duration rendering #### Singular minute rendering 62 hours and 1 minute — singular "minute" selected correctly for count 1 9 hours and 0 minutes — plural "minutes" for 0 61 hours and 6 minutes, 48 hours and 54 minutes, 14 hours and 27 minutes ## Related Issue https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5833 ## Other

## Summary

The patient chart's "Upcoming appointments" card sometimes rendered the same appointment twice.

`usePatientAppointments` derives `todaysAppointments` and `upcomingAppointments` from the same source array using overlapping filters:

- `upcomingAppointments` → `startDateTime` `isAfter(now)`
- `todaysAppointments` → `startDateTime` `isToday()`

An appointment scheduled **later today** (after the current moment) satisfies *both* conditions, so it appears in both lists. The card concatenated the two lists without deduping (`todaysAppointments.concat(futureAppointments)`), causing such appointments to render twice. Appointments dated tomorrow or earlier today were unaffected, which is why duplication only showed up "some of the time for some of the appointments".

This PR dedupes the combined list by `uuid` so each appointment renders exactly once. The fix is scoped to the card component; the resource hook's semantics are left unchanged because `patient-appointments-detailed-summary.extension.tsx` relies on today's appointments appearing in `upcomingAppointments` for its "Upcoming" tab.

## Screenshots

I can’t seem to visually replicate this anymore for some reason.

[No Jira ticket.](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5731)

Added `patient-upcoming-appointments-card.test.tsx` with two cases:

title: (fix) O3-5730: Automatically check in patient after starting a visit
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number.
- [x] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below.
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

When a scheduled patient has no active visit, clicking **Check in** opens the start visit workspace instead of checking them in directly. Previously, once the visit was created and the workspace closed, the appointment status was **not** updated — so the user had to click **Check in** a second time (now that an active visit exists) to actually check the patient in.

This PR wires the start visit workspace's `onVisitStarted` callback to set the appointment status to `CheckedIn` automatically. The patient is now checked in as soon as the visit is created, with no second click.

### Guarding against a double check-in

When patient-chart's `showUpcomingAppointments` is enabled, the visit form renders an "upcoming appointments" card. If the user selects the appointment there, the form checks it in via its own `onVisitCreatedOrUpdated` callback **before** `onVisitStarted` fires. Our auto check-in would then try to set `CheckedIn` a second time, which the backend rejects — the `DefaultAppointmentStatusChangeValidator` in `openmrs-module-appointments` disallows a `CheckedIn -> CheckedIn` transition (`toStatus.getSequence() <= currentStatus.getSequence()`).

To avoid this, the auto check-in first reads the appointment's current status (`GET /appointment?uuid={uuid}`) and skips the status change if it is already `CheckedIn`. If the status cannot be read, it attempts the check-in anyway rather than silently skipping it.

Implementation notes:
- Extracted the status-change + snackbar logic into a small local `checkIn(successSubtitle)` helper, reused by both the existing-active-visit path and the new auto-check-in path.
- The `customUrl` override and the existing-active-visit behavior are unchanged.
- Because the visit form only invokes `onVisitStarted` after a **successful** visit creation, a failed visit creation leaves the appointment status unchanged.

Added `checkin-button.test.tsx` covering:
- `customUrl` configured → navigates, does not change status or launch the workspace
- active visit exists → checks in directly, no workspace
- no active visit → launches the workspace but does not check in yet
- visit creation fails (`onVisitStarted` never fires) → appointment status unchanged
- visit started successfully (status not `CheckedIn`) → appointment status changes to `CheckedIn` and visits are mutated
- visit form already checked the appointment in (status `CheckedIn`) → auto check-in is skipped
- appointment status cannot be read → check-in is attempted anyway

body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration. - [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary Several notable fixes for the compact-patient-search component: * Previously, each call to `useSWRInfinite()` was, in essence, returning new copies of existing data, which lead to unnecessary re-renders. This has been fixed by setting `keepPreviousData` to `true` * Previously, when `useSWRInfinite()` set `isLoading` to `true`, all results were replaced with placeholder. Since this gets set to `true` even when, e.g., loading a second page of results, this resulted in unnecessary unmounts and recreations, which was both a memory leak and lead to a stampede of requests. * All search results were previously rendered and retained. This leads to stampedes of secondary queries (e.g., for patient photos, queue status, visit status, etc.). Instead, this PR moves us to using list virtualization so that roughly 10-18 items are retained in a React query. Large scrolls backwards or forwards have some slight glitches as components are re-rendered, but the easiest way to fix this is in the components rendering the secondary queries themselves. * Recent patients, however, are not virtualized at all, as we rely on this being a limited list that is safe to load. * A mistake in the call to `useArrowNavigation()` resulted in the arrow keys only being usable for up to the number of `recentPatients` * This PR adds additional component-level memoization where it makes sense to speed up rendering. In addition, in the context of search results, we re-tune SWR to more aggressively cache so that there's less need to re-try, e.g., patient photo queries * Additionally, this PR makes two fixes the service queues banner tag. First, if it is rendered outside the patient chart, a wrapper component is used so no query needs to be issued. Second, the query that was used overfetched data, especially as the queue details in the modal are basically reloaded, so the representation has been updated to minimize the data requested. This is one of the biggest contributing components. ## Screenshots This illustrates the trade-off here. Note the white patches while rows are reloading: ## Related Issue https://issues.openmrs.org/browse/O3-5714 ## Other Follow-ups: * ~~New billing PAID bill needs same wrapper treatment as queues app~~ [PR 749](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-billing-app/pull/749) * Active Visit tag needs SWR tweak * Might do small rework on central components in styleguide

## Summary

Adopts the happy-dom-by-default pattern that `openmrs-esm-core` already uses across its 25 per-package vitest configs, with per-file `/** @vitest-environment jsdom */` docblocks as the escape hatch for tests that hit happy-dom/jsdom divergences. See [`esm-navigation/src/history/history.test.ts`](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core/blob/e1470604dafd40c0e687b75b8838278061c511db/packages/framework/esm-navigation/src/history/history.test.ts#L2) in core for the established precedent.

### Changes
- `tools/vitest.shared.ts`: `environment: 'jsdom'` → `'happy-dom'`.
- `package.json`: add `happy-dom@^20.0.0`. Keep `jsdom@^28.0.0` because twelve test files in this repo still need it via the docblock escape hatch.
- Add `/** @vitest-environment jsdom */` to twelve test files where the form-submit flow under test does not fire its callback under happy-dom (a DOM-event-dispatch divergence around React Hook Form / Carbon `Form` submit handlers):
  - `esm-appointments-app/.../appointments-form.test.tsx`
  - `esm-bed-management-app/.../bed-form.workspace.test.tsx`
  - `esm-patient-registration-app/.../patient-registration.test.tsx`
  - `esm-patient-search-app/.../compact-patient-search.test.tsx`
  - `esm-patient-search-app/.../patient-search-bar.test.tsx`
  - `esm-patient-search-app/.../advanced-patient-search.test.tsx`
  - `esm-patient-search-app/.../refine-search.test.tsx`
  - `esm-service-queues-app/.../queue-room-form.test.tsx`
  - `esm-service-queues-app/.../queue-form.test.tsx`
  - `esm-ward-app/.../admit-patient-form.test.tsx`
  - `esm-ward-app/.../cancel-admission-request.test.tsx`
  - `esm-ward-app/.../notes.test.tsx`

### Why bother

jsdom's per-file environment init is the dominant fixed cost when vitest spawns a worker per test file; happy-dom roughly halves it. Benchmarks on `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/esm-patient-chart-app` (similar suite shape) showed a 29% wall-clock reduction. happy-dom's transitive dep tree is also smaller.

Single-line change:

body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

`useAppointmentList` was sending `forDate` as a UTC ISO timestamp via `dayjs(date).startOf('day').toISOString()`. For users in timezones east of UTC this produces the *previous* calendar day. At UTC+3, selecting 2026-04-18 produces `2026-04-17T21:00:00.000Z`.

The backend's `convertToLocalDateFromUTC` parses `forDate` with a `SimpleDateFormat` pattern that has no timezone token, so it reads the literal date/time digits and queries the wrong day. As a result, the daily appointments list can come back empty even when appointments exist for the selected date.

Format the value with `omrsDateFormat` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.SSSZZ`) so the sent string reflects local midnight (e.g. `2026-04-18T00:00:00.000+0300`) and the backend reads the intended date.

## Requirements
- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number.

## Summary

In `patient-admit-or-transfer-request-form.component.tsx`, the `finally` block had two issues:

1. `wardPatientGroupDetails.mutate()` was called without `await` — SWR cache invalidation fired and was forgotten, causing unreliable ward list re-renders and potential unhandled rejections if the component unmounted mid-mutation.

2. `setIsSubmitting(false)` ran before `mutate()` resolved — the submit button re-enabled while the mutation was still in-flight, allowing a user to submit again before the ward list refreshed and risking duplicate transfer requests.

The correct pattern already exists in `admit-patient-button.component.tsx` in the same repo. This component had diverged from it.

**Fix:** Changed the `finally` block to await the mutation before resetting submit state:
```ts
.finally(async () => {
  await wardPatientGroupDetails?.mutate?.();
  setIsSubmitting(false);
});
```
